newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Aygaz aims to double turnover.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Aygaz aims to double turnover.

text.p: Turkey's leading liquid petroleum gas (LPG) retailer and distributor Aygaz A.S. aims to more than double its turnover in 1997, a company official said.
"We aim to raise 1997 turnover by more than 100 percent to 62.75 trillion lira, from 29.5 trillion lira in 1996," Husrev Elveris, planning and quality manager of the company, told Reuters.
In U.S. dollars, the company's 1996 sales were $370 million.
Aygaz shares listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange traded at 24,000 lira on Monday morning, up from 22,250 lira at Friday's close.

Aygaz exceeded its original 1996 turnover target by 4.5 trillion lira, Elveris said, adding that they were also expecting pre-tax 1996 profits to exceed the original target by 450 to 500 billion lira.
"The rise in our 1996 net profits will be bigger than the increase in pre-tax profits because of certain tax exemptions due to investments," he added.
Elveris said the LPG sector in Turkey showed higher-than-expected growth in 1996 and the positive conditions would continue in 1997.
"Our target is to increase our overall market share to 37 percent by the year 2000 by maintaining our present growth rate, 35 percent in calor gas and 40 percent in bulk LPG," he said.

The company's total market share was 34.5 percent in 1996. It was followed by Ipragaz with 24-25 percent and Demiroren group with 14-15 percent. The rest is divided among several other companies, including Aygaz subsidiary Mogaz with a 4.5 percent share. Mogaz was bought from Mobil Oil Turkey in 1995.
Aygaz's sales rose by 12 percent to a total of 885,000 tonnes in 1996.
As for the company's 1997 sale targets, Elveris said: "The optimistic sales target is one million tonnes and the pessimistic target is 950,000 tonnes."
The annual filling capacity of Aygaz stands at 910,000 tonnes, under a single shift operation. Capacity utilisation was 83 percent last year.
Elveris said they would be able to meet this year's one-million-tonne target by increasing shifts to 1.5 or two.
"We do not need any additional capacity expansion investments," Elveris said, adding that eight trillion lira of investments were planned for 1997.
The company's total investment spending was 3.5 trillion lira in 1996, including a bulk LPG tanker purchased from Japan for 1.7 trillion lira.
Elveris said natural gas, the newcomer to the market, did not have any negative effects on LPG sales in Turkey, contrary to expectations.
"Because the annual population growth rate of the country is still running at 1.7 percent and is not expected to go down to below one percent before the year 2007," he said.

"But even if the population growth rate is reduced to zero, welfare will increase which means that the LPG market will continue to grow. So we do not expect any saturation in the market by the year 2010, at the earliest," Elveris added.
He said Aygaz would afterwards turn to new areas with the help of its flexible structure.
The company reported 18.75 trillion lira of turnover and 2.49 trillion lira of net profits in the first nine months of 1996, against 7.37 trillion and 649 billion lira in the same 1995 period.
